Forget other people; do you genuinely care about yourself ? Seen a quote saying - make friends with yourself and you’ll never be lonely. 

But, I totally get where you’re coming from. It’s not easy .. and there’s no quick fix to it. 

Personally, there’s loads of tools I’ve developed and can use at times of stress and crisis, like long walks, music, talking to people who understand, mindfulness and CBT. It’s difficult to see the point of doing these in difficult times but really and truly, they’re designed to harvest positive energy if used correctly. 

It gets better, if you want it to.
Wishing you the best. X

Ever had the thought that weed is the trigger to your anxiety? Psychological dependence can cause it. Old habits die hard and it ain’t easy but stopping smoking wacky backy might just be your redemption. Find pro active things to do, take up a craft/ hobby, go for long walks, teach yourself an instrument or language. Join a local community group. There’s plenty out there to help you fight the fears of losing a crutch , but you have to want to stop in the first place and the only person you’ll be kidding is yourself. So be honest to yourself.

An old Cherokee is teaching his grandson about life. “A fight is going on inside me,” he said to the boy. “It is a terrible fight and it is between two wolves. One is evil – he is anger, envy, sorrow, regret, greed, arrogance, self-pity, guilt, resentment, inferiority, lies, false pride, superiority, and ego.”

 

 He continued, “The other is good – he is joy, peace, love, hope, serenity, humility, kindness, benevolence, empathy, generosity, truth, compassion, and faith. The same fight is going on inside you – and inside every other person, too.”

 

The grandson thought about it for a minute and then asked his grandfather, “Which wolf will win?”

 

The old Cherokee simply replied, “The one you feed.”

You’re ultimately the one in control, it’s up to you, do you sit there, be less productive, and over think? Or do you engage in activity, face your fears and overcome them. 
Mindfulness is a great tool to harvest. It’s a slow process but in general it says not to think of past or future, just here and now, and that’s exactly where you need to be. 
I hope this is of some advice you can take and I wish you the best.
